U1 measurement · os-dev `session_01MbmmTHFS1B1rgE6n8npUPN` for the epic seat (`session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3`) · 2026-10-22T23:00Z · read-only, against `origin/main` `09e07c259a`. ## 1. Where the customer's state lives, per access type, and how the post-boot registry is read

**The registry read (all four types).** The one catalog read is `createSecurityCatalogReader` / `securityCatalogReaderOf(engine)` (`packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts`): engine registry first, then the metadata service. Every entry carries `packageId` (the definition's `_packageId`) when a package ships it, and none for an environment-authored item (a clone included). An outage throws `AuthzStoreUnavailableError`, never "absent". Declared sharing rules are not a catalog type: they are read from the registry's `sharing_rule` items by plugin-sharing's `createDeclaredSharingRuleSource` (`declared-sharing-rules.ts:272`), each carrying `packageId`. All of it is complete at `kernel:bootstrapped`, where `catalog-reference-report.ts` already runs (`security-plugin.ts:4736`).

| type | switch-off (ledger) | clones | assignments / references |
|---|---|---|---|
| permission set | `sys_metadata_activation` rows `metadata_type='permission'`; read today only name-bounded (`readDisabledCatalogNames`, `resolve-authz-context.ts:1112`) | environment-authored `permission` items in the catalog (no `packageId`), made by `POST /security/permission-sets/:name/clone` (`runtime/src/domains/permission-set-clone.ts`) | `sys_user_permission_set.permission_set`; position bodies' `permissionSets` |
| position | ledger rows `metadata_type='position'` | environment-authored `position` items | `sys_user_position.position` |
| sharing rule | ledger rows `metadata_type='sharing_rule'` (PR #24428, `964a23700f`), read by `readSwitchedOffDeclaredRules` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:1006`) | `sys_sharing_rule` rows (organization-owned; "rename the stored rule, which makes it a clone", `:991`) | the rule rows themselves (`object_name`, `criteria`) |
| capability | none: not an activation type (`catalog-activation.ts:84` lists position, permission, sharing_rule, webhook) | none: code-only (`allowRuntimeCreate: false`) | environment-authored sets' `systemPermissions` |

So U1 reads the ledger **whole** for the three ledger types (one system read, as `readSwitchedOffDeclaredRules` does), not through `readDisabledCatalogNames`.

## 2. How each finding kind is detected

- **Orphans.** A ledger row (any `active`) whose `(metadata_type, name)` the post-boot registry no longer resolves: `catalog.resolve(type, name)` for position / permission; the declared-rule list for `sharing_rule`. A switched-off orphan is the input to the next item; an orphan that is `active: true` is a dead row, reported as such.
- **Suspected re-enablements.** A switched-off orphan row whose `package_id` is P, plus every name of the same type that P now ships and that no ledger row names. Each finding names the old name, the candidate new name(s) and, for a permission set, the positions whose definition binds the candidate (the acceptance's "affected positions"); for a position, its holders' count is not needed, since a new position name has no assignment.
  - **What "the same package" can be read from:** the old side from the ledger row's `package_id` (written from the entry's `packageId` by `ObjectStoreMetadataActivationStore`, `metadata-activation-store.ts:272`); the new side from the catalog entry's `packageId` / the declared rule's `packageId`.
  - **What it cannot be read from:** a ledger row with no `package_id` (an environment-authored item, or any row written without one: the row-identity index is bare `(metadata_type, name)`, `sys-metadata-activation.object.ts:189`, and `package_id` is compared by no reader); and **any clone**, which by ADR-0126 §9 carries no package and no link to its base (`permission-set-clone.ts` rule 2). Nor is a *version* recorded anywhere at boot: "arrived" can only mean "shipped now by P with no ledger row", not "new in this upgrade". A package with several unswitched sets therefore yields several candidates, which is why the finding is "suspected".
  - **"The old name carrying a clone":** not readable at boot, because no clone records its base. The sanctioned ceremony is clone **plus** switch-off, so the switch-off half carries the finding. A clone with its base left on was not a choice the rename un-makes (the base and the clone both grant before and after).
- **Collisions.**
  - position / permission: a package name the environment catalog already holds **refuses the boot** (`refuseEnvironmentHeldSecurityCatalogNames`, `objectql/src/plugin.ts:1216`; ruling A on #22307), and package-vs-package and built-ins are refused at registration (`security-catalog-namespace.ts`). A boot that reaches `kernel:bootstrapped` holds none, so U1 reports none there; the pre-write check belongs to U2's door.
  - capability: code-only; the same registration refusal covers it.
  - sharing rule: a declared name held by a `sys_sharing_rule` row is **not** refused; it is served nowhere in that scope and logged lazily on the first serve (`reportDeclarationOverAuthoredRow`, `sharing-rule-service.ts:983`). U1 reports these at boot, per organization.
- **Clone bodies naming a missing object or field.** Environment-authored permission sets: `objects` keys and `fields` keys (`object.field`) checked against `engine.getObject(name)` and its field map; `systemPermissions` checked against `catalog.resolve('capability', …)` (this is the capability type's whole U1 surface). Environment-authored positions: `permissionSets` already reported by `catalog-reference-report.ts` item 4, so not duplicated. `sys_sharing_rule` rows: `object_name` and the field names in `criteria`.
- **Managed-set field denies that a same-object clone lacks.** For each package-shipped set M with `fields['o.f'].readable === false` (or `editable === false` where M grants edit on `o`), each environment-authored set C with an `objects.o` entry and no `fields['o.f']` entry. Unlisted fields are visible (`explain-engine.ts:886`), so C exposes `o.f`. With no clone linkage, "same-object" is read as "grants the same object", not "copied from M": it can list a customer set unrelated to M. Bounded (sets × denied fields), labelled as a review item, never acted on.

## 3. The administrator-visible channel

**There is no Setup health surface.** Setup's Diagnostics group holds Sessions and **Notification Events** (`platform-objects/src/apps/setup-nav.contributions.ts:149`), and every existing boot report is a server log line.

**The existing channel that fits: the notification ingress `messaging.emit()`** (ADR-0030; `service-messaging/src/messaging-service.ts:1088`). It writes the `sys_notification` event (listed in Setup → Diagnostics → Notification Events) and materialises the in-app inbox (the Console bell) for each recipient. `dedupKey` makes a repeat a no-op, so a stable key per finding set gives one notification per distinct set, not one per boot. No object, page, route or setting is added; the report emits one topic with `severity: 'warning'`.

**Recipients, and how "operator-gated under a wall" maps:**
- `single`: the administrator, i.e. the users the activation and clone doors admit: the holders of the Default Organization's `admin_full_access` grant (`readDefaultOrganizationId`, exported and read-only) plus any `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` address (`resolvePlatformAdminEmails`). The recipient resolver accepts both ids and email addresses.
- walled (`group` / `isolated`): **only** the configured `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` operator(s). The ledger and the catalog are deployment-level, and under a wall only the operator can switch or clone (`activation-gate.ts`, `walledCatalogWriteVerdict`), so no organization's administrator is told about a choice they cannot act on.
- No `messaging` service in the composition, or no recipient resolved: the server log says so once, naming the remedy (Absence must be loud). The log line is always written beside the notification, as `catalog-reference-report.ts` does.

## 4. `resolve-authz-context.ts`

**No change needed.** U1 imports `readDefaultOrganizationId` as it stands (read-only) and reads the ledger whole through the engine itself. It does not call `readDisabledCatalogNames` (name-bounded, position/permission only). #25248 / PR #25301 is not touched.

## 5. File surface and expected size

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/access-upgrade-report.ts` (new, beside `catalog-reference-report.ts`, same fail-closed shape: a read that did not happen stops the report and reports nothing past it): ~650 lines.
- `security-plugin.ts`: wiring at `kernel:bootstrapped` beside the catalog report, ~50.
- `plugin-sharing`: one public read on `SharingRuleService` returning the declared rules with `packageId` (the service is reached as `sharingRules` at bootstrapped; plugin-security keeps a structural type and gains no dependency), ~30.
- Tests: four types × (`single`, walled) × (finding, CONTROL), the fail-closed stop, the delivery and its absence, plus the ablation: ~1,300.
- One changeset: ~40.

**Expected: ~2,100–2,500 lines, under 3,000.** If it runs over, the cut is U1a (comparison + log report + pins) and U1b (the notification delivery + its pins).

## 6. Recommendation

Build as above: the comparison at `kernel:bootstrapped`, reported to the log and, through the existing notification ingress, to the administrator (`single`) or the operator only (walled). No new surface; no `resolve-authz-context.ts` change; nothing refused at boot. Two limits to accept, both forced by ADR-0126 §9 (no clone linkage) and by the bare `(metadata_type, name)` key: a re-enablement is "suspected" and can list several candidates, and the field-deny check reads "same object", not "copied from". Expected `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, re-declared from the diff (the topic id is a value on an existing channel, not a published key or setting; the seat may rule otherwise).

Everything else is built and green.

## What R4 measured

The showcase under production `os serve`, on a persistent SQLite database, in three boots per posture:
1. a clean boot;
2. the customer's switch-off of `showcase_auditor` recorded in `sys_metadata_activation` (`package_id` `com.example.showcase`), with the name still shipped: the **CONTROL**, which reports nothing;
3. the vendor renames the set to `showcase_audit_reader`, and its position `auditor` binds the new name.

The edits to the showcase's source, lockfile and `access-matrix.json` were local and temporary, and are reverted. The showcase also had to declare `@objectstack/organizations` temporarily, since no example app declares it and a walled serve refuses without it.

| posture | boot 3: detection | boot 3: delivery |
|---|---|---|
| `isolated` | ✅ `ERROR [security] 1 access item(s) the customer switched off are no longer shipped under that name…`, `showcase_auditor` → candidates incl. `showcase_audit_reader` (positions `["auditor"]`), plus 8 other same-package sets (the accepted "suspected" limit) | ❌ `messaging.emit()` refused: *"Insert on 'sys_notification' was REFUSED: a system-context write on a tenant-scoped object must carry an organization, and this install runs the 'isolated' tenancy posture…"* (ADR-0131 D9) |
| `group` | ✅ same | ❌ same refusal, `'group'` |
| `single` (for contrast) | ✅ same | ✅ one `sys_notification` row, topic `security.access_upgrade`, `organization_id` = the Default Organization, `dedup_key` `security.access_upgrade:<digest>` |

Under a wall there is no install organization, the operator belongs to none by design, and `sys_notification` and the inbox are tenant-scoped. So the notification family cannot hold a deployment-level event addressed to the operator. The report did fail loud (its "reached no administrator" error line), so nothing was silent. The unit and wiring pins could not see this, because they stub `messaging`.

## Options for the walled half (`single` is unaffected and stays as built)

- **A. Under a wall, the operator channel is the boot report's log line.** Recommended.
  - What changes: walled skips `emit()` and writes one `error` line addressed to the operator. It says the findings are deployment-level, that the operator alone can act, and that this posture has no in-app channel for them.
  - Surface and risk: no new surface, and nothing is written into any organization.
  - Cost: "administrator-visible" under a wall becomes the operator's server log, the same place every walled boot diagnostic already goes (`os serve` FATAL boxes, the walled posture lines).
- **B. Stamp the event with an organization the operator's account belongs to.**
  - What changes: look up the operator's `sys_user` by `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` and their `sys_member` organizations, and emit once per organization.
  - Surface and risk: no new surface. But it writes a deployment-level finding into a tenant organization's notification log, where that organization's administrators can read it. That breaks "operator-gated".
  - Cost: it delivers nothing when the operator has no membership.
- **C. Let the notification family carry a deployment-level event for a platform audience.**
  - What changes: `sys_notification`, delivery and inbox learn an organization-less, operator-only shape.
  - Surface and risk: it is a messaging and platform-objects change in ADR-0131 D9 territory, i.e. a new surface. It needs a ruling and its own card, outside U1.

**Recommendation: A in U1. C goes to its own card only if the maintainer wants the operator told in-app.** U2 is not affected: under a wall its refusal answers the operator, who is the caller at the install door.

## Two defects in my own code that R4 found, fixed with whichever option is chosen

- The undelivered line's fix text ("set OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL… compose the messaging service") is wrong when the cause is a refused write. The fix text will be per cause.
- The logger redacts the `dedupKey` meta field (`***REDACTED***`, a key-shaped name), so the digest will be logged under another name.

- **dispatch gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` gives 70 commands, each exit code captured before any pipe. 69 passed at first. The 70th, `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, exited 1 because this shallow clone lacked its pinned fixture commit; after fetching that one object it exits 0.
- **R1:** a fresh showcase boot under `single`. The report runs at `kernel:bootstrapped` with `absent: []` and finds nothing.
